transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because I just feel... worn down all the time. Like, not just “I had a busy week” tired, but this kind of constant low battery feeling. Even if I get what should be a full night’s sleep, I wake up and I’m still dragging, and then I have to get through work and whatever needs doing at home, and by the time I’ve dealt with all of that—especially just the house clutter and everyday stuff—I feel like there’s almost nothing left in me for anything else.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like, or has that changed recently?

Yeah… it’s changed. I wouldn’t say I never enjoy anything at all, because I can still sort of function and have normal conversations at work, and there are moments where something is fine, but most days there’s this low, gray feeling kind of running underneath everything.

Like, I used to get genuinely excited about baking, even just planning what to make or trying some little adjustment to a recipe, and now it feels more like… I know that’s something I used to like, but I don’t feel that same lift from it. Same with checking the telescope or nerding out about something in the lab — I can still do it, I can still talk about it, but it doesn’t feel light or satisfying the way it used to. It’s more muted, I guess. Like the volume got turned down on things that used to make me feel interested or happy.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It’s been… a little over two years, I think. It’s hard to put an exact date on it because it didn’t feel like one day I woke up and everything changed. It was more like this low baseline slowly became the normal background.

But if I trace it back, it started not long after we moved into the older house. At first I thought it was just the move, or the adjustment, or being tired from all the stuff that comes with an older place. But it just kind of… stayed. So, yeah, a little over two years now.
Do you often feel worthless or guilty about things?

I don’t know that I’d say “worthless,” exactly. That feels like a strong word. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, definitely, and I’ll think things like, “Why can’t I just handle this better?” or “Why is this so hard when other people seem to manage fine?” But I’m not sure if that’s the same thing as feeling worthless.

Guilt… maybe sometimes, but not in a big dramatic way. More like I feel bad when I’m not keeping up with things the way I think I should, or when I feel like I’m not being as present or useful as I want to be. But I don’t sit there thinking I’m a terrible person or anything. It’s more… disappointment in myself, I guess, or irritation with myself. I’m not sure if that’s what you mean.
Have you had thoughts about death or dying at any point since you started feeling this way?

Um… I don’t think so. Not in the sense of actually wanting to die, if that’s what you mean. I mean, I’ve had moments where I’m tired of feeling like this, and I’ll think something like, “I just want a break from my own head,” but it doesn’t turn into picturing myself dead or wishing I wouldn’t wake up or anything like that.

I guess death is one of those things that crosses your mind in an abstract way sometimes, like when you hear about someone getting sick or there’s something in the news, but since this started, I haven’t been sitting around thinking about dying as a solution or making plans or anything. It’s more… I get worn down and discouraged, but not in that direction.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?

I’m not sure I’d describe it that way, exactly. I mean, I get tense sometimes, like anyone does, and I can overthink things, but I don’t know if I’m walking around feeling anxious or on edge most of the time.

It’s more like… I feel kind of weighed down or slowed down than keyed up, if that makes sense. I’m not usually jumpy or panicky or constantly expecting something bad to happen. There are moments where I’m irritable or kind of braced for things, but I haven’t really thought of anxiety as the main thing. So… no, I don’t think often, unless I’m missing what you mean by “on edge.”
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since you started feeling this way?

Not really, no. I mean, my weight sort of goes up and down a little in the normal way, like depending on how busy I am or what I’ve been eating, but I haven’t noticed anything I’d call significant.

I’m not someone who tracks it super closely every day, so I suppose it’s possible there’s been a small change, but my clothes fit about the same, and nobody has commented on it or anything. So… no, I don’t think there’s been a major weight change since I started feeling this way.
Do you still find pleasure in social interactions or has that also become less enjoyable for you?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because it sort of depends on the person and the situation. I don’t think I’ve stopped enjoying people altogether, no. Like, if I’m with someone I’m comfortable with and the conversation is easy, I can still laugh or feel glad I went.

But I do think sometimes it takes more effort to get myself there, if that makes sense. The actual social interaction can be okay once I’m in it, but before it happens I might think, “Ugh, do I have the energy for this?” And if it’s a bigger group or something where I have to be “on,” that can feel less appealing than it used to.

So… I wouldn’t say social interactions are completely not pleasurable. They can still be nice. It’s just not always as automatic, maybe, or I don’t look forward to them as much every time.
Do you often feel sad or empty most of the day?

Yeah… I think so. Not every single minute in a dramatic way, but most days there’s this kind of low, gray feeling in the background. Like I can still get up and go to the lab, talk to people, do what I’m supposed to do, so from the outside I probably seem basically fine. But internally it’s like the color’s been turned down a little.

I don’t know if I’d always call it “sad,” exactly. Sometimes it’s more empty, or flat, or just… heavy. I used to get more naturally excited about little things, like baking something on a weekend or checking the telescope and feeling that spark of curiosity. I can still do those things, but they don’t feel as light or satisfying as they used to. It’s more like I’m going through the motions and waiting for that feeling to show up, and it doesn’t really.

So yes, I’d say most days, for a lot of the day, there’s that low mood there. It’s just not always obvious because I can still function around it.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy most of the time?

Yeah… I think I have, at least somewhat. It’s not like I’ve stopped doing everything I used to enjoy, but most days there’s this low, gray mood kind of running in the background, and it makes the things I used to look forward to feel less… bright, I guess.

Like, I can still go to the lab, I can talk to people, I can get through the day and do what needs doing. And I still technically like some of the same things — baking, for example, or checking on the telescope, or just getting absorbed in something curious or hands-on. But the feeling I used to get from them isn’t as easy to access. I used to feel this little lift from those things, like a genuine spark of interest or comfort, and now it’s more muted.

So I wouldn’t say I have no interest at all. It’s more that I don’t feel light or excited about things the way I used to, and that’s there most days.
Have you had periods in the past where you felt significantly better than you do now, only to have these low feelings return?

Yeah… I mean, there have been better days or stretches where I’m distracted enough that it doesn’t feel as noticeable, but if you mean like a real period where I felt back to my old self for a while and then it came back, I don’t think so, not really.

It feels more like this lower baseline has just been there for a long time. I started noticing it shortly after we moved into the older house, and that was a little over two years ago now. At first I thought it was just the stress of the move, or settling in, or maybe needing time to adjust, but then it didn’t really lift in the way I expected it to. It kind of became the background setting.

So I can have a decent week, or a good conversation, or a day where I’m productive and think, “Okay, maybe I’m fine,” but underneath that it still feels like the same lower level is there. I wouldn’t say it disappears for months and then returns. It’s more like it’s been pretty consistently there since around that time, just louder or quieter depending on the day.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months where you felt consistently better, without these low feelings, since they first started over two years ago?

No, I don’t think so. I’ve had better days, definitely, and maybe even little stretches where I was busy enough or things were going smoothly enough that I didn’t focus on it as much. But I can’t think of a full two months where I felt consistently back to normal, without that low feeling in the background.

It’s more like… since shortly after we moved into the older house — a little over two years ago — my baseline just shifted downward. Some days it’s quieter, and I can almost convince myself it’s not there, but when I really think about it, it hasn’t fully gone away for that long. It’s just been sort of steadily there, in different intensities.
Have you felt this low, gray mood for most of every day, nearly every day, since it started over two years ago?

Yeah… most days, yes. I don’t know if I’d say every single minute of every day, because I can get absorbed in work or a conversation and not be actively thinking, “I feel low right now.” But if I step back and look at the whole day, it’s usually there in the background.

It’s like this dull, gray layer over things. I can still go to the lab, do what I’m supposed to do, talk to people, answer emails, whatever. I’m functioning. But I don’t feel light, if that makes sense. Things that used to give me a little lift — baking something, checking on the telescope, getting curious about some small thing — they don’t land the same way. I’ll do them, and part of me knows I used to enjoy them more, but the feeling is kind of muted.

So, nearly every day, yes. It’s not always intense, and I can sometimes push it to the side, but it’s there most of the time.
Has there been any period since you first started feeling this way, over two years ago, where you felt completely back to your normal self for at least a few months?

No, I really don’t think there has been. I keep trying to think if there was some stretch where I felt fully like myself again, because there have been better weeks here and there, but not a few months where it was just gone.

This lower baseline started shortly after we moved into the older house, a little over two years ago, and it’s kind of just… stayed. It hasn’t been the exact same every day, but I wouldn’t say I ever got completely back to normal for months at a time.
Has your low mood been consistently present for the entire two years since it started, without any breaks or periods where it significantly improved?

Yes… I mean, as far as I can tell, it’s been there the whole time. It started not long after we moved into the older house — a little over two years ago now — and since then it’s like my normal level just dropped and never really came back up.

There have been days where I’m distracted or things feel a little easier, so I don’t want to make it sound like every single day has been exactly the same. But I can’t point to any real break where it significantly lifted and stayed lifted. It’s more like it’s always been sitting underneath everything, sometimes stronger, sometimes quieter, but still there.
Have you noticed if your low mood tends to worsen or improve at specific times of the year?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed a clear seasonal pattern, honestly. I’ve tried to think about that because it seems like the kind of thing that might make sense — like winter being worse or summer being better — but I can’t really point to a specific time of year where it reliably shifts.

There are days or weeks that feel a little heavier or a little easier, but I haven’t connected that to the seasons in any consistent way. It’s more like this same background low feeling just sort of continues through the year, and other things might make it feel louder or quieter, but I don’t think I’ve seen a predictable yearly cycle.
Has your low mood ever significantly improved for a period of time since it started, only to return later?

Not really, no. I mean, it has had little ups and downs, so there have been times where I might have said, “Okay, this week is a little better,” or I was functioning a bit more normally. But I wouldn’t say it significantly improved and then came back later, like a clear break.

It’s more that this lower baseline started shortly after we moved into the older house, a little over two years ago, and it’s just kind of been the floor I’ve been living on since then. Sometimes it feels less noticeable, but I don’t think it ever really lifted in a way that felt like I was back to myself and then relapsed.
Has your low mood been present every day for the past two years without any significant breaks or improvements?

Yes, basically… I know I keep circling back to the same thing, but the clearest way I can describe it is that my baseline dropped shortly after we moved into the older house, and that was a little over two years ago now. Since then it’s felt like that lower level has just been there.

I wouldn’t want to claim every single day has been identical, because some days I’m more distracted or I can get through things a little more easily, but I can’t think of any meaningful stretch where it really went away or where I felt like I was back to how I used to be. It’s more like it’s been this ongoing background state the whole time.
Has there been any two-year period since you first started feeling this way where your low mood significantly improved?

No, I don’t think so. Since it first started, it’s really just been this same lower baseline. Like I’ve said, it seemed to begin not long after we moved into the older house, and that was a little over two years ago now.

There have been days where I function better or where it’s not as much in the front of my mind, but I wouldn’t call that a significant improvement. I can’t point to any two-year stretch, or even a meaningful long stretch inside that time, where it lifted and stayed better. It’s more like it settled in around then and has just continued.
Has your low mood been present for the entire two years without any period where it significantly improved and stayed better for at least a few months?

Yes… as far as I can tell, yes. It’s been there the whole time in that sense. I keep thinking back and trying to be fair about it, because I don’t want to exaggerate and say every day was exactly the same, but the low baseline itself started not long after we moved into the older house, and that was a little over two years ago now.

There have been better days, sure, or days where I was more occupied and maybe didn’t notice it as sharply. But I can’t remember a period of a few months where it actually lifted and stayed better, like I returned to normal for a while. It’s more like it settled in back then and just never really left.
